                endpoint:
                  type: string
                  description: "Governed runtime URL agents MUST call. Per-wire-format path (e.g. .../mcp/<alias> for gateway-fronted agents, or the AgentCore Runtime ARN for direct-runtime agents). Status-driven discovery clients read THIS, not upstreamEndpoint, to stay on the governed path."
                # Per-scope governed endpoint map {scope: url} the operator publishes
                # via the shared perimeter-URL helper. Open object (dynamic scope keys)
                # — declared so K8s does not silently strip the operator's write.
                endpoints:
                  type: object
                  description: "Per-scope governed endpoint URLs the operator resolved for this asset. The single best one is mirrored to status.endpoint."
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                upstreamEndpoint:
                  type: string
                  description: "Raw provider URL behind the gateway (AgentCore Runtime ARN / Gateway MCP URL). Diagnostics only — agents that call this directly bypass MoDaaS governance and provider-agnostic guardrail enforcement."
                # ── Global Resource Endpoint + scope ──
                globalResourceEndpoint:
                  type: string
                  format: uri
                  description: |

Stable, externally-resolvable URL representing the governance perimeter
                    for this asset. Set by the operator on transition to Approved. Immutable
                    thereafter. Format: https://<gateway-host>/<wire-format>/<asset-uid>.
                endpointScope:
                  type: string
                  enum: [mesh, vpc, public]
                  description: |
                    Resolvable scope of globalResourceEndpoint. mesh = cluster-internal only;
                    vpc = VPC-internal; public = externally addressable.
                componentRef:
                  type: object
                  description: "Canvas Component CR that owns this asset (set by operator after Component emission)."
                  properties:
                    name:
                      type: string
                    namespace:
                      type: string
                    uid:
                      type: string
                tmf639Resource:
                  type: object
                  description: "TMF639 v5 Resource Inventory record this asset projects to."
                  properties:
                    id:
                      type: string
                      description: "Stable TMF639 resource ID."
                    url:
                      type: string
                      format: uri
                      description: "Direct URL to the TMF639 record (e.g., RI baseUrl + /resource/{id})."
                audit:
                  type: object
                  description: "Addressable audit pointers for this asset."
                  properties:
                    logGroup:
                      type: string
                      description: "CloudWatch log group name."
                    queryUrl:
                      type: string
                      format: uri
                      description: "Pre-built CloudWatch Logs Insights query URL."
                # ── Governance approval audit trail ──
                governance:
                  type: object
                  description: "Governance approval state, Reviewing → Approved gate."
                  properties:
                    approvals:
                      type: array
                      description: "Append-only list of signed approval attestations."
                      items:

type: object
                        required: [subject, role, at]
                        properties:
                          subject: { type: string, maxLength: 253 }
                          role: { type: string, maxLength: 253 }
                          attestation: { type: string, maxLength: 2048 }
                          signature: { type: string, maxLength: 4096 }
                          at: { type: string, format: date-time }
                    awaitingSince:
                      type: string
                      format: date-time
                      nullable: true
                    rejectedAt:
                      type: string
                      format: date-time
                      nullable: true
                    rejectedReason:
                      type: string
                      maxLength: 256
                conditions:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: object
                    required: [type, status]
                    properties:
                      type: { type: string }
                      status: { type: string, enum: ["True", "False", "Unknown"] }
                      reason: { type: string }
                      message: { type: string }
                      lastTransitionTime: { type: string, format: date-time }
                dependencyStatus:
                  type: object
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                # ── `dependencyHealthy` is written by the operator (cascade
                # observability) and MUST be declared in the schema, otherwise
                # K8s silently strips the boolean.
                dependencyHealthy:
                  type: boolean
                  description: "Cascade observability — top-level convenience scalar mirroring the DependencyHealthy condition. True iff every dependency has reached its kind's serving state (ModelConfig: Approved — models have no Active phase; ToolConfig: Active)."
                # ── Agent-Action Policy status mirror ──
                # The operator publishes the engine selected, the PDP location,
                # readiness of the PDP, and lightweight decision counters for
                # observability. The schema declares the block so K8s does not
                # silently strip operator writes.

agentPolicy:
                  type: object
                  description: "Agent-action policy status mirror. Populated by the agent operator when spec.agentPolicy is declared (agent-action policy contract)."
                  properties:
                    engineKind:
                      type: string
                      enum: [cedar, opa, avp, webhook, none]
                      description: "Engine the operator resolved from spec.agentPolicy.engine.kind."
                    pdpKind:
                      type: string
                      enum: [inCluster, avp, agentCoreAuth, opa, webhook, none]
                      description: "Effective PDP backend (Cedar inCluster/avp/agentCoreAuth, or the engine kind itself for non-Cedar)."
                    pdpReady:
                      type: boolean
                      description: "True when the PDP backend has loaded the projected policy and is reachable."
                    projectedConfigMap:
                      type: string
                      maxLength: 253
                      description: "Name of the projected ConfigMap in modaas-system that the PDP consumes (Cedar inCluster path)."
                    lastValidatedAt:
                      type: string
                      format: date-time
                      description: "Timestamp of the last successful policy syntax validation."
                    lastDecision:
                      type: object
                      description: "Lightweight policy-decision counters (populated once agent-action-policy wiring is in place)."
                      properties:
                        allowed:
                          type: integer
                          minimum: 0
                        denied:
                          type: integer
                          minimum: 0
                        lastEvaluatedAt:
                          type: string
                          format: date-time
      subresources:
        status: {}
      additionalPrinterColumns:
        - { name: Agent,    type: string,  jsonPath: .spec.agentName }
        - { name: Provider, type: string,  jsonPath: .spec.provider }
        - { name: Phase,    type: string,  jsonPath: .status.phase }
        - { name: Paused,   type: boolean, jsonPath: .spec.paused, priority: 1 }

# ModelConfig — Open-contract CRD for ODA Canvas model lifecycle
# =============================================================================
# Namespace-scoped CRD declaring one foundation model's identity, capabilities,
# safety intent, governance metadata, and provider-specific configuration.
#
# Provider-agnostic at the root; provider-specific only within typed sub-blocks.
# CEL rules enforce exactly-one typed block matching spec.provider, plus
# immutability of the identity triple {alias, provider, modelId}.
#
# Extension protocol for new providers: add one typed sub-block + one CEL rule
# pair (requirement + exclusivity). No fork, no second CRD.
# =============================================================================
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: modelconfigs.oda.tmforum.org
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: modaas-canvas
  annotations:
    oda.tmforum.org/crd-version: "v1beta1"
    # Declarative spec lineage — ties this CRD to the TMF specification it
    # realizes, the way ODA Canvas CRDs cite TMF6xx / SID. This is the first
    # concrete implementation of GB1085 §4 Canvas Operator Requirements.
    oda.tmforum.org/spec-sdo: "TMForum"
    oda.tmforum.org/specification: "GB1085 Model-as-a-Service v1.0.0"
    oda.tmforum.org/spec-section: "GB1085 §2.2 + §4"
    oda.tmforum.org/governed-asset: "model"
spec:
  group: oda.tmforum.org
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: modelconfigs
    singular: modelconfig
    kind: ModelConfig
    shortNames: [mc]
  conversion:
    strategy: None
  versions:
    # ── legacy alpha versions: not served by default (kept here for migration) ──
    - name: v1alpha1
      served: false
      storage: false
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
      subresources:
        status: {}
    - name: v1alpha2
      served: false
      storage: false
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
      subresources:
        status: {}
    # ── current storage version ──
    - name: v1beta1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object

description: "Governs one foundation model (LLM) as a declarative Kubernetes resource: onboarding, safety/guardrail intent, lifecycle (approve/pause/retire), and publication to a discovery catalog. An operator reconciles this spec against a backing provider (AWS Bedrock by default; others pluggable via sibling operators, no CRD change). Agents reach the model through the MoDaaS AI Gateway — a reverse-proxy pod that enforces this asset's policy on every call (see status.endpoint). Runs on ODA Canvas, TM Forum's open telco-platform framework; this realizes GB1085 §2.2 (service functionality) + §4 Canvas Operator Requirements. TMF639/SID references are optional standards metadata."
          required: ["spec"]
          x-kubernetes-validations:
            # ── Governance Approval Gate invariants ──
            # 1. Approval count gate: phase=Approved requires at least
            #    requiredApprovals signed attestations when approval is required.
            - rule: |
                !has(self.status) || !has(self.status.phase) || self.status.phase != 'Approved'
                || !has(self.spec.governance) || !has(self.spec.governance.approval)
                || !has(self.spec.governance.approval.required)
                || self.spec.governance.approval.required != true
                || (has(self.status.governance) && has(self.status.governance.approvals)
                    && size(self.status.governance.approvals) >=
                       (has(self.spec.governance.approval.requiredApprovals) ? self.spec.governance.approval.requiredApprovals : 1))
              message: "phase=Approved with governance.approval.required=true requires at least requiredApprovals signed attestations in status.governance.approvals[] (governance approval gate)."
            # 2. Safety-required assets must opt INTO approval gating.
            #    Grandfather: this is a TRANSITION rule — it demands approval
            #    only when the safety posture is NEWLY set on create, or when
            #    spec.safety changes on update. A pre-existing CR whose safety
            #    block is unchanged is grandfathered, so admission never rejects
            #    an already-Approved asset on operator status-touch or annotate
            #    re-apply (admission fires before the operator's grandfather
            #    check can run).
            - rule: |

!(has(self.spec.safety) && has(self.spec.safety.required) && self.spec.safety.required == true)
                || (oldSelf.hasValue() && has(oldSelf.value().spec.safety) && oldSelf.value().spec.safety == self.spec.safety)
                || (has(self.spec.governance) && has(self.spec.governance.approval)
                    && has(self.spec.governance.approval.required)
                    && self.spec.governance.approval.required == true)
              optionalOldSelf: true
              message: "spec.safety.required=true demands spec.governance.approval.required=true — no silent auto-approve; pre-existing assets with unchanged safety are grandfathered (governance approval gate)."
            # 3. Approver role match: every approval record's role must match
            #    spec.governance.approval.approverRole when explicitly set.
            - rule: |
                !has(self.status) || !has(self.status.governance)
                || !has(self.status.governance.approvals)
                || !has(self.spec.governance) || !has(self.spec.governance.approval)
                || !has(self.spec.governance.approval.approverRole)
                || self.status.governance.approvals.all(a, !has(a.role) || a.role == self.spec.governance.approval.approverRole)
              message: "every status.governance.approvals[].role must match spec.governance.approval.approverRole (governance approval gate)."
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              description: "Desired state of the governed model: identity (alias/provider/modelId), capabilities, safety enforcer, governance, and provider-specific config."
              required: ["alias", "provider", "modelId"]
              x-kubernetes-validations:
                # ── Credential handling: referenced, never inline ──
                # Admission rules enforce that API_KEY/OAUTH assets reference a Secret;
                # credential material is never carried inline in the resource.
                - rule: "!(self.credentialProviderType in ['API_KEY','OAUTH']) || (has(self.credentialSecretRef) && self.credentialSecretRef != '')"
                  message: "credentialProviderType API_KEY or OAUTH requires spec.credentialSecretRef — credentials are REFERENCED from a Secret, never inline"

# A secret ref with no credential type is a contradiction: it declares a credential the
                # system will never load, which reads as configured auth while none is in force.
                - rule: "!has(self.credentialSecretRef) || self.credentialSecretRef == '' || self.credentialProviderType in ['API_KEY','OAUTH']"
                  message: "spec.credentialSecretRef is set but credentialProviderType is NONE/providerManaged — the secret would never be loaded"
                # ── Requirement rules: declared provider MUST have its block ──
                - rule: "self.provider != 'aws-bedrock' || has(self.awsBedrock)"
                  message: "provider=aws-bedrock requires spec.awsBedrock block"
                - rule: "self.provider != 'aws-sagemaker' || has(self.awsSageMaker)"
                  message: "provider=aws-sagemaker requires the spec.awsSageMaker block (SageMaker provider)"
                - rule: "self.provider != 'azure-openai' || has(self.azureOpenAI)"
                  message: "provider=azure-openai requires spec.azureOpenAI block"
                - rule: "self.provider != 'google-vertex' || has(self.googleVertex)"
                  message: "provider=google-vertex requires spec.googleVertex block"
                - rule: "self.provider != 'databricks' || has(self.databricks)"
                  message: "provider=databricks requires spec.databricks block"
                - rule: "self.provider != 'nvidia-nim' || has(self.nvidiaNIM)"
                  message: "provider=nvidia-nim requires spec.nvidiaNIM block"
                - rule: "self.provider != 'ollama' || has(self.ollama)"
                  message: "provider=ollama requires spec.ollama block"
                - rule: "self.provider != 'custom' || has(self.custom)"
                  message: "provider=custom requires spec.custom block"
                # ── Exclusivity rules: no other provider's block may be present ──
                - rule: "self.provider == 'aws-bedrock' || !has(self.awsBedrock)"
                  message: "spec.awsBedrock only allowed when provider=aws-bedrock"
                - rule: "self.provider == 'aws-sagemaker' || !has(self.awsSageMaker)"
                  message: "spec.awsSageMaker only allowed when provider=aws-sagemaker"
                - rule: "self.provider == 'azure-openai' || !has(self.azureOpenAI)"

message: "spec.azureOpenAI only allowed when provider=azure-openai"
                - rule: "self.provider == 'google-vertex' || !has(self.googleVertex)"
                  message: "spec.googleVertex only allowed when provider=google-vertex"
                - rule: "self.provider == 'databricks' || !has(self.databricks)"
                  message: "spec.databricks only allowed when provider=databricks"
                - rule: "self.provider == 'nvidia-nim' || !has(self.nvidiaNIM)"
                  message: "spec.nvidiaNIM only allowed when provider=nvidia-nim"
                - rule: "self.provider == 'ollama' || !has(self.ollama)"
                  message: "spec.ollama only allowed when provider=ollama"
                - rule: "self.provider == 'custom' || !has(self.custom)"
                  message: "spec.custom only allowed when provider=custom"
                # ── Provider-locked enforcer kinds ──
                # bedrockGuardrail (in-Converse) requires Bedrock; cross-provider
                # safety must use bedrockGuardrailExternal.
                # The operator already refuses this — admission catches it earlier
                # so users see the violation at apply-time.
                - rule: "!has(self.safety) || !has(self.safety.enforcer) || self.safety.enforcer.kind != 'bedrockGuardrail' || self.provider == 'aws-bedrock'"
                  message: "safety.enforcer.kind=bedrockGuardrail (Bedrock-native, in-Converse) requires provider=aws-bedrock; use bedrockGuardrailExternal for other providers (provider-agnostic guardrail)"
                # ── Immutability of identity triple ──
                # Once created, these cannot change. Governance: approver signed
                # off on this specific tuple; changing would invalidate approval
                # and orphan registry records.
                - rule: "oldSelf.alias == self.alias"
                  message: "spec.alias is immutable after creation"
                - rule: "oldSelf.provider == self.provider"
                  message: "spec.provider is immutable after creation"
                - rule: "oldSelf.modelId == self.modelId"
                  message: "spec.modelId is immutable after creation"
                # registryRef selects the discovery-catalog backing (Registry CR).
                # Immutable after creation: silently re-homing an asset's records

# to a different catalog would orphan the prior registry's records
                # and break audit provenance (same governance rationale as the
                # identity triple). Optional set-once field: may be set later if absent at create, never removed or re-pointed.
                - rule: "!has(oldSelf.registryRef) || (has(self.registryRef) && oldSelf.registryRef == self.registryRef)"
                  message: "spec.registryRef is immutable once set (removing or re-pointing it would orphan the prior catalog's records)"
                # ── Endpoint semantics ──
                # aws-bedrock: endpoint optional (operator derives from region).
                # All other providers: endpoint required (no region-derivation path).
                - rule: "self.provider == 'aws-bedrock' || has(self.endpoint)"
                  message: "spec.endpoint is required for all providers except aws-bedrock (which derives from region)"
              properties:
                # ── Identity ──
                alias:
                  type: string
                  description: "Stable, human-friendly model name that consumers reference (e.g. an agent calls 'noc-llm', not the raw provider model id). Immutable after creation; resolved by the gateway to the provider modelId at invocation time."
                  pattern: "^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$"
                  maxLength: 63
                  minLength: 1
                  example: noc-llm
                provider:
                  type: string
                  # OPEN CONTRACT: provider is an open pattern, NOT a closed enum.
                  # Eight typed provider blocks ship with paired
                  # requirement/exclusivity CEL (aws-bedrock + aws-sagemaker wired in the
                  # AWS reference operator; azure-openai/google-vertex/databricks/
                  # nvidia-nim/ollama/custom are contract-ready for sibling operators).
                  # A new provider adds one typed block + one CEL pair — no CRD fork.
                  # The CEL rules short-circuit on `provider != <block>`, so an
                  # unenumerated provider with no typed block validates and is owned by
                  # whichever sibling operator recognizes it (community scope).
                  pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
                  default: aws-bedrock

description: "Model backing provider. Open contract: aws-bedrock + aws-sagemaker ship in the AWS reference operator; azure-openai, google-vertex, databricks, nvidia-nim, ollama, custom are contract-ready; sibling operators add more without a CRD bump. example: aws-bedrock"
                  example: aws-bedrock
                modelId:
                  type: string
                  description: "Provider-native model identifier the alias resolves to (e.g. a Bedrock foundation-model id or inference-profile id). Immutable after creation. Interpreted per spec.provider."
                  minLength: 1
                  maxLength: 253
                  example: "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0"
                # ── Declarative spec lineage (TMF/GB1085 conformance anchor) ──
                # Optional. Lets a reviewer statically map this CR to the TMF spec
                # section it realizes — the way ODA Canvas CRs cite TMF6xx / SID
                # entities. Pure metadata; no operator behavior depends on it.
                specLineage:
                  type: object
                  description: "Declarative TMF specification lineage for this asset (conformance anchor; ref: GB1085 §4)."
                  properties:
                    sdo: { type: string, default: "TMForum", example: "TMForum" }
                    specification: { type: string, example: "GB1085 Model-as-a-Service v1.0.0" }
                    section: { type: string, example: "§2.2.6 Active Content Guardrails" }
                    sidEntity: { type: string, example: "LogicalResource" }
                # ── Runtime endpoint (provider-neutral, top-level) ──
                # Per the composition principle, endpoint answers one
                # provider-neutral question — "where does the
                # AI Gateway Pod route this model's inference traffic?". It belongs
                # at the top of spec, not nested inside provider blocks.
                #
                # For provider=aws-bedrock: optional. If unset, the operator derives
                # from spec.awsBedrock.region (https://bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com)
                # and writes the result to status.endpoint. Set explicitly only for
                # PrivateLink/VPC interface endpoints, FIPS, or custom routing.
                #

# For all other providers: required (enforced via CEL below).
                endpoint:
                  type: string
                  format: uri
                  description: >
                    Runtime endpoint URL for the Gateway Pod to route inference traffic.
                    Optional for provider=aws-bedrock (derived from awsBedrock.region);
                    required for all other providers.
                description:
                  type: string
                  description: "Free-text, human-readable description of this model and its intended use; surfaced in discovery catalogs and the registry record."
                  maxLength: 512
                paused:
                  type: boolean
                  default: false
                  description: "If true, operator halts reconciliation (quarantine/debug)"

# ── Capability declaration ──
                # ── Registry reference ──
                # Points to a Registry CR that selects the backing catalog.
                # Optional — defaults to the annotated default Registry in
                # the operator namespace. Follows K8s PVC.storageClassName /
                # Ingress.ingressClassName convention.
                registryRef:
                  type: object
                  description: "Reference to the Registry CR that this asset publishes to."
                  properties:
                    name:
                      type: string
                      maxLength: 253
                    namespace:
                      type: string
                      default: "modaas-system"
                      maxLength: 63
                capabilities:
                  type: object
                  description: >
                    Capability declaration for agent discovery and routing.
                    features[] is the single source of truth — polycapable
                    models list all capabilities they support simultaneously.
                  properties:
                    features:
                      type: array
                      description: "All capabilities this model supports simultaneously"
                      items:
                        type: string
                        enum:
                          - chat
                          - reasoning
                          - embedding
                          - vision
                          - tool-use
                          - streaming
                          - code-generation
                          - structured-output
                          - audio
                          - time-series
                          - rerank
                    modalities:
                      type: array
                      items: { type: string, enum: [text, image, audio, video] }
                    minContextWindow:
                      type: integer
                      minimum: 1
                      description: "Minimum viable context window in tokens"
                    maxContextWindow:
                      type: integer
                      minimum: 1
                      description: "Model's hard maximum context window"
                    supportedMediaTypes:
                      type: array

description: "MIME types the model accepts"
                      items:
                        type: string
                        pattern: "^[a-z]+/[a-zA-Z0-9.+-]+$"
                    regions:
                      type: array
                      items: { type: string }
                    tier:
                      type: string
                      enum: [economy, standard, premium, frontier]

# ── Safety (intent + policy reference) ──
                safety:
                  type: object
                  description: "Content-safety governance for this model. Declares whether safety enforcement is required and which enforcer realizes it (e.g. a provider-native guardrail). Admission rejects a self-contradictory posture (e.g. required=true with enforcer.kind=none)."
                  properties:
                    required:
                      type: boolean
                      default: false
                    policyRef:
                      type: object
                      description: "Typed reference (K8s objectReference convention). Kept for backward compatibility; prefer `safety.enforcer` for new configs."
                      required: [kind, name]
                      properties:
                        kind:
                          type: string
                          enum: [ConfigMap, BedrockGuardrail, SafetyPolicy, ExternalRef]
                        name: { type: string, minLength: 1 }
                        namespace: { type: string }
                    # ── Safety Enforcement Abstraction ──
                    # Pluggable enforcer contract. The AI Gateway dispatches on
                    # enforcer.kind at invocation time; operators dispatch at
                    # reconcile time. When absent, behavior falls back to legacy
                    # implicit bedrockGuardrail path (backward compat for
                    # existing CRs that use awsBedrock.guardrails).
                    enforcer:
                      type: object
                      description: "Safety enforcer. If omitted and safety.required=true with provider=aws-bedrock, legacy awsBedrock.guardrails path is used."
                      properties:
                        kind:
                          type: string
                          enum: [bedrockGuardrail, bedrockGuardrailExternal, gatewayFilter, external, none]
                          description: "Enforcement mechanism. bedrockGuardrail=Bedrock-native in-Converse (provider=aws-bedrock only); bedrockGuardrailExternal=Bedrock ApplyGuardrail standalone (any provider); gatewayFilter=MoDaaS-internal (deferred); external=customer service; none=opt-out (only valid when safety.required=false)."
                        # ── Enforcement driver axis (orthogonal to `kind`) ──

# `kind` = WHAT kind of enforcement; `enforcedAt` = WHICH driver
                        # realizes it. self = the MoDaaS AI Gateway (default, current
                        # behavior). Other values federate to an external enforcement
                        # driver behind the EnforcementDriver SPI (reserved for future
                        # sibling implementations; the self/reference path is what ships
                        # today). Additive: omitting it defaults to `self`, so existing
                        # CRs are unchanged.
                        enforcedAt:
                          type: string
                          pattern: "^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$"
                          # OPEN driver axis (SPI): NOT a closed enum, so a new
                          # enforcement driver (Kong AI Gateway, Envoy AI Gateway, …)
                          # federates without a CRD bump. Known values: self (MoDaaS AI
                          # Gateway, default), agentgateway (Linux Foundation), muleSoftAiGateway
                          # (the last two are reserved for future sibling implementations;
                          # the self/reference path is what ships today).
                          # The operator refuses a CR naming a driver it has no code for
                          # (refuse-before-approve, parity with the gateway version-skew guard).
                          default: self
                          example: self
                          description: "Enforcement driver — which gateway governs this asset's boundary. self=MoDaaS AI Gateway (default, the path that ships today); agentgateway=Linux Foundation agentgateway; muleSoftAiGateway=MuleSoft AI Gateway (these external drivers are reserved for future sibling implementations). Orthogonal to provider: names WHO enforces, not where the model lives."
                        bedrockGuardrail:
                          type: object
                          description: "For kind=bedrockGuardrail. References or inlines Bedrock guardrail spec. If omitted, awsBedrock.guardrails is used (legacy path)."
                          x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                        # ── Standalone Bedrock guardrail (provider-agnostic) ──
                        bedrockGuardrailExternal:
                          type: object

description: "For kind=bedrockGuardrailExternal. Bedrock guardrail invoked via ApplyGuardrail API, decoupled from model invocation. Works for any provider (SageMaker, Ollama, vLLM, Databricks). The guardrail itself is still a Bedrock control-plane resource."
                          properties:
                            guardrailId:
                              type: string
                              description: "Bedrock guardrail identifier (BYO). When omitted, operator provisions one from awsBedrock.guardrails inline policy."
                            guardrailVersion:
                              type: string
                              default: "DRAFT"
                              description: "Guardrail version to apply. Defaults to DRAFT."
                            applyTo:
                              type: array
                              description: "Enforcement directions: input (filter prompt before invoke), output (filter completion before return)."
