                          role:
                            type: string
                            description: "Realm role the approver wielded; matches spec.governance.approval.approverRole."
                            maxLength: 253
                          attestation:
                            type: string
                            description: "Free-form rationale text (audit)."
                            maxLength: 2048
                          signature:
                            type: string
                            description: "Optional detached signature over (subject, role, at). MUST NOT contain reusable credential material such as bearer tokens or JWTs with live audiences — status is readable by any principal with get on the CR. Full signature verification reserved for a future iteration."
                            maxLength: 4096
                          at:
                            type: string
                            format: date-time
                            description: "ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of approval."
                    awaitingSince:
                      type: string
                      format: date-time
                      description: "Wall-clock time the CR entered Reviewing; cleared on Approved."
                      nullable: true

- { name: Scope, type: string, jsonPath: .status.endpointScope, priority: 1 }

- { name: Age,      type: date,    jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp }

---
# =============================================================================
# Registry CRD v1beta1
# Data-only CRD — no reconcile loop. Referenced by ModelConfig/ToolConfig/
# AgentConfig via spec.registryRef.name. Asset operators resolve references at
# reconcile time and dispatch to the correct backing plugin.
#
# Follows K8s precedent: StorageClass (provisioner+parameters), IngressClass
# (controller field filter), GatewayClass (controllerName + parametersRef).
# =============================================================================
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: registries.oda.tmforum.org
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: modaas
    oda.tmforum.org/component-type: governance
  annotations:
    modaas.tmforum.org/design-pattern: "k8s-storageclass-ingressclass-gatewayclass"
spec:
  group: oda.tmforum.org
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: registries
    singular: registry
    kind: Registry
    shortNames: [reg]
  versions:
    - name: v1beta1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          description: "Selects WHERE governed assets (ModelConfig/ToolConfig/AgentConfig) publish their discovery records — the backing-selector for MoDaaS, following the Kubernetes StorageClass / IngressClass pattern. NOT a fourth governed asset: it picks a catalog backing (AWS Agent Registry, Canvas TMF639 Resource Inventory, or an in-memory stub) and the operator dispatches projection through the matching plugin. An asset's registryRef names a Registry; that Registry's `backing` decides which catalog the record lands in. Realizes GB1085 §4 Registration-and-Discovery (optional pattern)."
          required: [spec]
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              required: [controller, backing]
              # ── Admission invariants. A contributed CRD must carry
              #    admission-safety CEL, not just shape. Registry is the
              #    StorageClass-pattern backing-selector; like StorageClass's
              #    immutable provisioner, controller+backing are fixed after
              #    creation (re-pointing a Registry's backing would silently
              #    re-home every asset that references it). ──
              x-kubernetes-validations:

- rule: "oldSelf.controller == self.controller"
                  message: "spec.controller is immutable after creation (re-homing a Registry's owning operator is not a safe in-place mutation; create a new Registry instead)"
                - rule: "oldSelf.backing == self.backing"
                  message: "spec.backing is immutable after creation (changing the backing would orphan every asset that published to the old backing; create a new Registry instead)"
                # Known backings that require connection parameters must declare them.
                # in-memory is the only known backing that needs none. Unknown
                # (third-party) backings are unconstrained — sibling operators own them.
                - rule: "self.backing != 'agentcore' || has(self.parameters)"
                  message: "backing=agentcore requires spec.parameters (e.g. registryName, region)"
                - rule: "self.backing != 'tmf639' || has(self.parameters)"
                  message: "backing=tmf639 requires spec.parameters (e.g. baseUrl)"
              properties:
                controller:
                  type: string
                  description: |
                    Controller identifier that owns this Registry, following
                    the IngressClass/GatewayClass precedent. Operators filter
                    by this field and ignore Registries owned by others.
                    Example: 'aws-model-operator.modaas' (reference impl).
                  pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,127}$"
                  maxLength: 128
                backing:
                  type: string
                  description: |
                    Registry backing implementation identifier. The operator
                    dispatches to the backing plugin registered under this key.
                    Known values: 'agentcore' (AWS AgentCore Registry),
                    'tmf639' (Canvas TMF639 Resource Inventory v5 peer),
                    'in-memory' (test double).
                    Third parties register their own via sibling operators.
                  pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$"
                  maxLength: 64
                parameters:
                  type: object
                  description: |
                    Free-form backing-specific parameters (StorageClass

convention). Pass-through to the backing plugin.
                    Common keys by backing:
                      agentcore: {registryName, region, roleArn?}
                      tmf639:    {baseUrl, timeout?}
                      in-memory: {}
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                description:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 512
            status:
              type: object
              properties:
                phase:
                  type: string
                  enum: [Ready, Degraded, Unreachable, Unknown, ReadOnly]
                  description: "Observed reachability — written by periodic health probe if enabled. ReadOnly indicates a read-only backing (e.g. a TMF639 Resource Inventory peer view) that is reachable but does not accept record writes."
                lastProbed:
                  type: string
                  format: date-time
                recordCount:
                  type: integer
                  description: "Observed count of APPROVED records in this backing (probe filters by approval state). For a read-only backing (e.g. a TMF639 Resource Inventory peer view) this reflects what the peer exposes, which may not be the full set."
                message:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 1024
              x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
      subresources:
        status: {}
      additionalPrinterColumns:
        - { name: Controller, type: string, jsonPath: .spec.controller }
        - { name: Backing,    type: string, jsonPath: .spec.backing }
        - { name: Phase,      type: string, jsonPath: .status.phase }
        - { name: Records,    type: integer, jsonPath: .status.recordCount, priority: 1 }
        - { name: LastProbed, type: date,   jsonPath: .status.lastProbed,   priority: 1 }
        - { name: Age,        type: date,   jsonPath: .metadata.creationTimestamp }

# ToolConfig — Open-contract CRD for ODA Canvas tool lifecycle
# =============================================================================
# Namespace-scoped CRD declaring one MCP tool server's identity, endpoint,
# tool schemas, access controls, and provider-specific configuration.
#
# Provider-agnostic at the root; provider-specific only within typed sub-blocks.
# CEL rules enforce exactly-one typed block matching spec.provider, plus
# immutability of the identity pair {toolName, provider}.
#
# Extension protocol: add one typed sub-block + one CEL rule pair.
# =============================================================================
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: toolconfigs.oda.tmforum.org
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: modaas-canvas
  annotations:
    oda.tmforum.org/crd-version: "v1beta1"
    # Declarative spec lineage — ties this CRD to the TMF specification it
    # realizes, the way ODA Canvas CRDs cite TMF6xx / SID. MoDaaS is the first
    # concrete implementation of GB1085 §4 Canvas Operator Requirements.
    oda.tmforum.org/spec-sdo: "TMForum"
    oda.tmforum.org/specification: "GB1085 Model-as-a-Service v1.0.0"
    oda.tmforum.org/spec-section: "§4 Canvas Operator Requirements (tool registration + Canvas MCP)"
    oda.tmforum.org/governed-asset: "tool"
spec:
  group: oda.tmforum.org
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: toolconfigs
    singular: toolconfig
    kind: ToolConfig
    shortNames: [tc]
    categories: [oda, modaas]
  conversion:
    strategy: None
  versions:
    - name: v1beta1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object

description: "Registers one backend (an AWS Lambda, HTTP API, or MCP server) as a governed tool that AI agents may call, and manages its lifecycle (onboarding, access policy, retirement). MCP = Model Context Protocol, the open JSON-RPC standard agents use to discover and invoke tools. An operator reconciles this spec against a backing gateway (AWS Bedrock AgentCore Gateway by default — an AWS managed service that fronts tool backends for agents) and publishes a discovery record. Open contract: provider is an open pattern, not a fixed enum — sibling operators add Databricks/MuleSoft/etc. without a CRD change. Runs on ODA Canvas (TM Forum's open telco-platform framework); realizes GB1085 §4 Canvas Operator Requirements (tool registration + Canvas MCP)."
          required: ["spec"]
          x-kubernetes-validations:
            # Governance approval gate invariants
            # Gate fires on EVERY serving phase: this kind's phase machine has a
            # distinct Active (deployed/serving) state past Approved — without it
            # in the trigger, a status writer could reach a serving state having
            # never satisfied the approval gate. (ModelConfig has no Active phase;
            # its gate correctly triggers on Approved alone.)
            - rule: |
                !has(self.status) || !has(self.status.phase)
                || !(self.status.phase in ['Approved', 'Active'])
                || !has(self.spec.governance) || !has(self.spec.governance.approval)
                || !has(self.spec.governance.approval.required)
                || self.spec.governance.approval.required != true
                || (has(self.status.governance) && has(self.status.governance.approvals)
                    && size(self.status.governance.approvals) >=
                       (has(self.spec.governance.approval.requiredApprovals) ? self.spec.governance.approval.requiredApprovals : 1))
              message: "a serving phase (Approved/Active) with governance.approval.required=true requires at least requiredApprovals attestations in status.governance.approvals[] (governance approval gate)."
            # Grandfather transition rule — demands approval only when the safety
            # posture is newly set (create) or changed (update). Pre-existing CRs
            # with unchanged safety are grandfathered, so admission never rejects

# an already-Approved asset on re-apply (admission fires before the
            # operator's approval check can run).
            - rule: |
                !(has(self.spec.safety) && has(self.spec.safety.required) && self.spec.safety.required == true)
                || (oldSelf.hasValue() && has(oldSelf.value().spec.safety) && oldSelf.value().spec.safety == self.spec.safety)
                || (has(self.spec.governance) && has(self.spec.governance.approval)
                    && has(self.spec.governance.approval.required)
                    && self.spec.governance.approval.required == true)
              optionalOldSelf: true
              message: "spec.safety.required=true demands spec.governance.approval.required=true — no silent auto-approve; pre-existing assets with unchanged safety are grandfathered (governance approval gate)."
            - rule: |
                !has(self.status) || !has(self.status.governance)
                || !has(self.status.governance.approvals)
                || !has(self.spec.governance) || !has(self.spec.governance.approval)
                || !has(self.spec.governance.approval.approverRole)
                || self.status.governance.approvals.all(a, !has(a.role) || a.role == self.spec.governance.approval.approverRole)
              message: "every status.governance.approvals[].role must match spec.governance.approval.approverRole (governance approval gate)."
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              description: "Desired state of the governed tool: identity (toolName/provider), tool contract type, backing, access/PDP policy, and provider-specific config."
              required: ["toolName", "provider"]
              x-kubernetes-validations:
                # ── Requirement rules: declared provider MUST have its block ──
                - rule: "self.provider != 'agentCoreGateway' || has(self.agentCoreGateway)"
                  message: "provider=agentCoreGateway requires spec.agentCoreGateway block"
                - rule: "self.provider != 'custom' || has(self.custom)"
                  message: "provider=custom requires spec.custom block"
                # ── Exclusivity rules: no other provider's block may be present ──
                - rule: "self.provider == 'agentCoreGateway' || !has(self.agentCoreGateway)"

message: "spec.agentCoreGateway only allowed when provider=agentCoreGateway"
                - rule: "self.provider == 'custom' || !has(self.custom)"
                  message: "spec.custom only allowed when provider=custom"
                # ── Immutability ──
                - rule: "oldSelf.provider == self.provider"
                  message: "spec.provider is immutable after creation"
                - rule: "oldSelf.toolName == self.toolName"
                  message: "spec.toolName is immutable after creation"
                # registryRef selects the discovery-catalog backing (Registry CR).
                # Immutable after creation: silently re-homing an asset's records
                # to a different catalog would orphan the prior registry's records
                # and break audit provenance. Optional set-once field: may be set later if absent at create, never removed or re-pointed.
                - rule: "!has(oldSelf.registryRef) || (has(self.registryRef) && oldSelf.registryRef == self.registryRef)"
                  message: "spec.registryRef is immutable once set (removing or re-pointing it would orphan the prior catalog's records)"
                # ── Cross-vendor neutrality rules (v1beta1 additive) ──
                - rule: "!has(self.credentialProviderType) || self.credentialProviderType == 'NONE' || self.credentialProviderType == 'providerManaged' || self.credentialProviderType == 'GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE' || (has(self.credentialSecretRef) && self.credentialSecretRef != '')"
                  message: "credentialProviderType=API_KEY|OAUTH requires a non-empty credentialSecretRef pointing to a Kubernetes Secret (NONE/providerManaged/GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE are broker-injected, no secretRef needed)"
                - rule: "!has(self.toolType) || self.toolType != 'openapi' || has(self.backendRef)"
                  message: "toolType=openapi requires backendRef (typically an s3:// URI to OpenAPI spec)"
                - rule: "!has(self.toolType) || self.toolType != 'smithy' || has(self.backendRef)"
                  message: "toolType=smithy requires backendRef (typically an s3:// URI to Smithy IDL)"
                - rule: "!has(self.toolType) || self.toolType != 'function' || has(self.backendRef) || has(self.agentCoreGateway) || has(self.custom)"

message: "toolType=function requires a backing — backendRef (e.g. a Lambda ARN) or a provider block (agentCoreGateway/custom) that resolves the function target"
              properties:
                # ── Identity ──
                toolName:
                  type: string
                  description: "Stable, human-friendly tool name that agents reference when invoking this tool. Immutable after creation; together with provider forms the identity pair."
                  pattern: "^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$"
                  maxLength: 63
                  minLength: 1
                  example: aws-docs-helper
                provider:
                  type: string
                  # OPEN CONTRACT (parity with AgentConfig): provider is an open
                  # pattern, NOT a closed enum. The AWS reference operator handles
                  # `agentCoreGateway`; sibling operators register additional providers
                  # (databricks, muleSoftFlexGateway, Kong/Apigee, …) with NO CRD bump.
                  # The requirement/exclusivity CEL rules short-circuit on
                  # `provider != <block>`, so an unenumerated provider carrying no
                  # typed block validates and is simply ignored by operators that don't
                  # own it. `custom` remains the inline escape hatch.
                  pattern: "^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$"
                  default: agentCoreGateway
                  description: "Backing provider for this tool. Open contract: agentCoreGateway (AWS reference) + custom (inline escape) ship today; sibling operators add providers (e.g. databricks, muleSoftFlexGateway) without a CRD change. example: agentCoreGateway"
                  example: agentCoreGateway
                # ── Declarative spec lineage (TMF/GB1085 conformance anchor) ──
                specLineage:
                  type: object
                  description: "Declarative TMF specification lineage for this asset (conformance anchor; ref: GB1085 §4)."
                  properties:
                    sdo: { type: string, default: "TMForum", example: "TMForum" }
                    specification: { type: string, example: "GB1085 Model-as-a-Service v1.0.0" }
                    section: { type: string, example: "§4 Canvas Operator Requirements" }

sidEntity: { type: string, example: "LogicalResource" }
                description:
                  type: string
                  description: "Free-text, human-readable description of this tool and its intended use; surfaced in discovery catalogs and the registry record."
                  maxLength: 512
                paused:
                  type: boolean
                  default: false
                  description: "When true, the operator withdraws the tool's serving path so consumers can no longer invoke it (a soft kill-switch); the CR is retained for audit and can be un-paused."

# ── Safety attestation (approval default-flip; AgentConfig alignment) ──
                # A tool attests whether it handles safety-sensitive data/actions.
                # safety.required=true flips governance.approval.required on by
                # default (the operator reads spec.safety.required for every kind).
                # Tools do NOT enforce model guardrails — that is
                # AgentConfig.safety.enforces. This block is the tool-side
                # attestation, kept shape-consistent with ModelConfig.safety.required
                # for cross-CRD uniformity.
                safety:
                  type: object
                  description: "Tool safety attestation. Drives the approval default-flip."
                  properties:
                    required:
                      type: boolean
                      default: false
                      description: "When true, this tool handles safety-sensitive data or performs sensitive actions; opts the tool into the governance approval gate by default."
                    # ── Enforcement driver axis ──
                    # ToolConfig already carries credential fields
                    # (credentialProviderType/credentialSecretRef). enforcedAt names
                    # which driver governs MCP/tool calls. agentgateway +
                    # muleSoftAiGateway have the richest MCP policy suites, so the tool
                    # path is their strongest fit.
                    enforcedAt:
                      type: string
                      pattern: "^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$"
                      default: self
                      example: self
                      description: "Enforcement driver for tool/MCP calls. self=the platform's own gateway enforces inline (default); agentgateway/muleSoftAiGateway federate enforcement to an external driver (reserved for future sibling implementations; the self/reference path is what ships today)."

# ── Cross-vendor neutrality fields (v1beta1 additive) ──
                # These fields keep the contract provider-neutral: governance is
                # declared once and applies regardless of which backend serves the tool.
                # ── Registry reference ──
                # Points to a Registry CR that selects the backing catalog.
                # Optional — defaults to the annotated default Registry in
                # modaas-system. Follows K8s PVC.storageClassName /
                # Ingress.ingressClassName convention.
                registryRef:
                  type: object
                  description: "Reference to the Registry CR that this asset publishes to."
                  properties:
                    name:
                      type: string
                      maxLength: 253
                    namespace:
                      type: string
                      default: "modaas-system"
                      maxLength: 63
                toolType:
                  type: string
                  enum: [mcp, openapi, smithy, function]
                  default: mcp
                  description: "Type of tool contract (MCP-aligned). Operator uses this with backendRef to project provider-specific config."
                backendRef:
                  type: string
                  minLength: 1
                  maxLength: 2048
                  description: "Opaque backend reference interpreted by provider. Examples: Lambda ARN, HTTPS URL, s3://bucket/key URI."
                outputSchema:
                  type: object
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                  description: "JSON Schema for tool result (MCP outputSchema equivalent). Enables response validation and tool-selection reasoning."
                annotations:
                  type: object
                  description: "Behavior annotations (MCP-aligned). Governance can route policy based on these."
                  properties:
                    readOnly:
                      type: boolean
                      default: true
                      description: "Tool does not modify state (safe by default)"
                    idempotent:
                      type: boolean
                      default: true
                      description: "Repeated calls with same input produce same result"

destructive:
                      type: boolean
                      default: false
                      description: "Tool performs irreversible operations (deletes, sends email, etc.)"
                credentialProviderType:
                  type: string
                  # The NEUTRAL credential vocabulary is provider-agnostic.
                  # `providerManaged` is the abstract "the
                  # broker injects an identity it manages" mode — each provider
                  # block realizes it (agentCoreGateway → GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE,
                  # a MuleSoft/Kong block → its own managed identity). The
                  # AWS-named GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE value is retained as a served,
                  # DEPRECATED alias so existing CRs keep validating; new CRs
                  # should use `providerManaged`. Default flipped from the
                  # AWS-named GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE to the neutral NONE so a non-AWS
                  # ToolConfig no longer silently carries an AWS credential mode.
                  enum: [NONE, providerManaged, API_KEY, OAUTH, GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE]
                  default: NONE
                  description: "Neutral credential scope policy. NONE | providerManaged (broker-injected identity) | API_KEY | OAUTH. GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE is a DEPRECATED AWS-named alias for providerManaged (agentCoreGateway). Type only — actual secret referenced by credentialSecretRef."
                credentialSecretRef:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 253
                  description: "Name of Kubernetes Secret holding credentials. Required (non-empty) when credentialProviderType is API_KEY or OAUTH; NONE, providerManaged and GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE are broker-injected and take no secretRef. Credentials NEVER inline in CRD."
                dependsOn:
                  type: object
                  description: "Cross-asset dependency declarations. Operator gates approval until all refs exist and are Approved."
                  properties:
                    models:
                      type: array
                      items:
                        type: string
                        pattern: "^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$"
                        maxLength: 63
                      maxItems: 10
description: "ModelConfig aliases this tool calls (for RAG/agent-in-tool patterns)"

# ── Governance ──
                governance:
                  type: object
                  description: "Governance metadata for this tool: ownership, data-classification, lifecycle/retirement, and the optional approval gate. Drives admission checks and the discovery-catalog record."
                  properties:
                    owner: { type: string }
                    costCenter: { type: string }
                    dataClassification:
                      type: string
                      enum: [public, internal, confidential, pii, regulated, restricted]
                    retirementDate:
                      type: string
                      format: date
                      description: "Planned retirement date. Operator transitions phase to Retired when reached."
                    # ── Governance approval gate ──
                    approval:
                      type: object
                      description: |
                        Human/policy approval gate. When required=true,
                        the AssetOperator parks the CR in phase=Reviewing until
                        a signed attestation from the role declared in
                        approverRole appears in status.governance.approvals[].
                        Default for required flips on spec.safety.required so
                        non-safety assets keep auto-approving.
                      properties:
                        required:
                          type: boolean
                          description: "When unset, defaults to spec.safety.required."
                        requiredApprovals:
                          type: integer
                          minimum: 1
                          default: 1
                        approverRole:
                          type: string
                          description: "FQN role name. Defaults to modaas-toolconfig-<toolName>-admin."
                          maxLength: 253

# ── Access control ──
                access:
                  type: object
                  description: "Authorization policy for invoking this tool: the Cedar policy that grants/forbids agent->tool calls and the PDP engine that enforces it. The tool side is the grant-capable (permit) authority for its actions."
                  x-kubernetes-validations:
                    # ── PDP policy-projection invariant ──
                    # agentPolicy.engine.cedar requires a grant-capable policy
                    # source. cedarPolicy is the inline grant-capable PRIMARY
                    # (resource side). If an agentPolicy.engine.cedar block is
                    # declared it must either carry an explicit policyId OR rely on
                    # cedarPolicy being present (policyId is then derived from the
                    # CR name by the operator).
                    - rule: |
                        !has(self.agentPolicy) || !has(self.agentPolicy.engine)
                        || !has(self.agentPolicy.engine.cedar)
                        || has(self.agentPolicy.engine.cedar.policyId)
                        || has(self.cedarPolicy)
                      message: "access.agentPolicy.engine.cedar requires either an explicit policyId or an inline access.cedarPolicy; policyId is derived from the CR name when unset (agent-action policy contract)."
                  properties:
                    requiredRole:
                      type: string
                      description: "Keycloak/Istio role required to invoke tools"
                    cedarPolicy:
                      type: string
                      description: |
                        Inline Cedar policy document — the grant-capable PRIMARY
                        (resource side). When present, the aws-tool-operator projects
                        this text into a label-scoped ConfigMap in modaas-system
                        (app.kubernetes.io/part-of=modaas-pdp) so the in-cluster PDP
                        hot-loads it, and the AI Gateway tool path calls
                        POST <pdp>/decide on every invocation, fail-closed (reserved
                        for future sibling implementations; the self/reference path is
                        what ships today). If access.agentPolicy.engine.cedar.policyId

is unset, the policyId is derived from the CR name
                        (modaas-toolconfig-<name>).
                    # ── PDP wiring (tool path policy enforcement) ──
                    agentPolicy:
                      type: object
                      description: |
                        Declares HOW the inline cedarPolicy is enforced at
                        runtime. Principal=agent (JWT sub / SigV4 identity),
                        action=invoke, resource=this tool. Optional — when omitted,
                        MoDaaS enforcement is off for this tool (default behavior
                        unchanged). Presence (alongside cedarPolicy) opts the tool
                        into PDP enforcement on the tool path.
                      properties:
                        engine:
                          type: object
                          description: "Policy engine selector. Only cedar is supported today."
                          properties:
                            cedar:
                              type: object
                              description: "Cedar PDP wiring for this tool."
                              properties:
                                pdpRef:
                                  type: string
                                  default: "modaas-pdp.modaas-system.svc.cluster.local:8080"
                                  maxLength: 253
                                  description: |
                                    Service reference to the in-cluster PDP.
                                    Defaults to the standard modaas-pdp ClusterIP.
                                    The AI Gateway calls POST http://<pdpRef>/decide.
                                policyId:
                                  type: string
                                  maxLength: 253
                                  description: |
                                    Explicit Cedar policyId the operator stamps on
                                    the projected ConfigMap and the gateway sends
                                    in the /decide request body. When unset, the
                                    operator derives it from the CR name
                                    (modaas-toolconfig-<name>) — see cedarPolicy.

# ── AgentCore Gateway (AWS reference) ──
                agentCoreGateway:
                  type: object
                  description: "Provider-specific configuration when provider=agentCoreGateway (the managed MCP gateway that fronts this tool backend). Exactly one provider block must match spec.provider (CEL-enforced)."
                  x-kubernetes-validations:
                    # A ToolConfig must EITHER adopt an existing target OR declare a
                    # backing. Valid backings:
                    #   - mcpServer (lambda ARN or http(s) URL with tools[] or native MCP)
                    #   - apiGateway (existing REST API)
                    #   - smithyModel (inline or s3)
                    #   - openApiSchema (inline or s3)
                    - rule: |
                        has(self.adoptTargetId)
                        || has(self.apiGateway)
                        || has(self.smithyModel)
                        || has(self.openApiSchema)
                        || has(self.tools)
                        || (has(self.mcpServer) && has(self.mcpServer.endpoint)
                            && (self.mcpServer.endpoint.startsWith("https://")
                                || self.mcpServer.endpoint.startsWith("http://")
                                || self.mcpServer.endpoint.startsWith("arn:aws:lambda:")))
                      message: "agentCoreGateway requires one of: adoptTargetId / apiGateway / smithyModel / openApiSchema / tools[] / mcpServer.endpoint=http(s)://|arn:aws:lambda:"
                    - rule: "!has(self.adoptTargetId) || has(self.gatewayIdentifier)"
                      message: "adoptTargetId requires gatewayIdentifier (which gateway hosts the adopted target)"
                    # Provider-mismatch could slip CEL because the backing-presence
                    # rule above was an OR across all backings. Tighten with
                    # per-backing structural invariants so that asserting a backing
                    # block actually means the block is valid.
                    # ── mcpServer must carry an http(s) endpoint or Lambda ARN when present ──
                    # Some ToolConfigs wrap Lambda backends and store the Lambda ARN
                    # in mcpServer.endpoint. A rule that required http(s):// alone

# rejected every status patch for those, freezing last-reconciled.
                    # Permit the arn:aws:lambda: prefix alongside http(s)://. Keep
                    # blocking obviously-broken values (ftp://, empty strings,
                    # malformed scheme) by requiring the endpoint to start with one of
                    # the three accepted prefixes.
                    - rule: "!has(self.mcpServer) || (has(self.mcpServer.endpoint) && (self.mcpServer.endpoint.startsWith('https://') || self.mcpServer.endpoint.startsWith('http://') || self.mcpServer.endpoint.startsWith('arn:aws:lambda:')))"
                      message: "agentCoreGateway.mcpServer requires endpoint starting with http://, https://, or arn:aws:lambda:"
                    # ── tools[], when declared, must be non-empty ──
                    # Empty arrays were slipping the OR-chain via has(self.tools)
                    # because CEL's has() returns true for [].
                    - rule: "!has(self.tools) || size(self.tools) > 0"
                      message: "agentCoreGateway.tools must contain at least one tool when declared (use adoptTargetId for managed-target adoption with no inline tools)"
                  properties:
                    # ── ADOPT MODE ──
                    # When adoptTargetId is set the operator does NOT create a
                    # new Gateway target. It reads the existing target by ID,
                    # writes observed tools to status, registers a Registry
                    # record, and never mutates or deletes the backing target.
                    # This makes the "zero-code governance overlay" thesis true
                    # for pre-existing Gateway deployments.
                    adoptTargetId:
                      type: string
                      description: |
                        Existing Gateway target ID to adopt. Operator never
                        creates, updates, or deletes this target. Use with
                        gatewayIdentifier to identify the host gateway.
                        Mutually exclusive with managed-mode (tools[] required)
                        in spec semantics though not CEL-enforced (tools[] can
                        still be declared for governance record documentation
                        even in adopt mode — observed tools from Gateway win).

minLength: 1
                    # ── END ADOPT MODE ──
                    # ─── credentialProviderConfigurations pass-through ───
                    # AgentCore Gateway supports 4 credential provider types for target
                    # invocation. Default GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE works for Lambda + native
                    # mcpServer targets; OAUTH and API_KEY unlock protected HTTP backends.
                    credentialProviderType:
                      type: string
                      enum: [GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE, OAUTH, API_KEY, JWT_PASSTHROUGH, CALLER_IAM_CREDENTIALS, NONE]
                      default: GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE
                      description: |
                        Credential provider AgentCore Gateway uses when invoking this target.

AWS-native values (passed through verbatim):
                          GATEWAY_IAM_ROLE        Gateway's own IAM role (default for Lambda)
                          OAUTH                   Registered OAuth provider ARN
                          API_KEY                 API key header/query param
                          JWT_PASSTHROUGH         Caller's JWT forwarded verbatim
                          CALLER_IAM_CREDENTIALS  Caller's IAM credentials forwarded

MoDaaS virtual value:
                          NONE  Omit credentialProviderConfigurations entirely. Valid
                                only for mcpServer targets against public no-auth
                                servers (e.g. aws-knowledge-mcp-server).
                    credentialProvider:
                      type: object
                      description: "Provider-specific credential configuration. Shape depends on credentialProviderType."
                      x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                      properties:
                        oauthCredentialProvider:
                          type: object
                          x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                          properties:
                            providerArn:
                              type: string
                              description: "ARN of the OAuth credential provider registered in AgentCore."
                            scopes:
                              type: array
                              items: { type: string }
                            grantType:
                              type: string
                              enum: [CLIENT_CREDENTIALS, AUTHORIZATION_CODE]
                        apiKeyCredentialProvider:
                          type: object
                          x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                          properties:
                            providerArn:
                              type: string
                              description: "ARN of the API key credential provider registered in AgentCore."
                            credentialParameterName:
                              type: string
                              description: "Name of the header/query param carrying the API key."
                            credentialLocation:
                              type: string
                              enum: [HEADER, QUERY]
                              default: HEADER
                    # ─── Explicit backing blocks ───
                    # AgentCore Gateway supports 5 native targetConfiguration.mcp types
                    # beyond mcpServer+lambda. These fields declare them explicitly so
                    # the operator doesn't have to infer from mcpServer.endpoint.
                    apiGateway:
                      type: object

description: |
                        Wrap an existing AWS API Gateway REST API as governed MCP tools.
                        Operator dispatches to targetConfiguration.mcp.apiGateway.
                      required: [restApiId]
                      properties:
                        restApiId:
                          type: string
                          description: "AWS API Gateway REST API id (e.g. abcd1234ef)"
                          minLength: 1
                        stage:
                          type: string
                          description: "API Gateway stage name. Default: prod."
                          default: prod
                        apiGatewayToolConfiguration:
                          type: object
                          description: "Optional per-tool overrides and path filters."
                          x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                    smithyModel:
                      type: object
                      description: |
                        Smithy-defined service. Inline JSON OR S3-backed model file.
                        Operator dispatches to targetConfiguration.mcp.smithyModel.
                      x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                      properties:
                        inlinePayload:
                          type: string
                          description: "Smithy model as inline JSON string."
                        s3:
                          type: object
                          properties:
                            uri: { type: string }
                            bucketOwnerAccountId: { type: string }
                    openApiSchema:
                      type: object
                      description: |
                        OpenAPI spec explicitly declared (separate from
                        mcpServer.endpoint inference). Inline JSON string OR S3.
                        Operator dispatches to targetConfiguration.mcp.openApiSchema.
                      x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                      properties:
                        inlinePayload:
                          type: string
                          description: "OpenAPI spec as inline JSON string."
                        s3:
                          type: object
                          properties:

uri: { type: string }
                            bucketOwnerAccountId: { type: string }
                    mcpServer:
                      type: object
                      description: |
                        Lambda ARN or remote http(s) MCP URL. Operator infers Lambda
                        vs native-mcpServer vs OpenAPI dispatch from the endpoint.
                        Not required if apiGateway/smithyModel/openApiSchema is declared.
                      properties:
                        endpoint:
                          type: string
                          minLength: 1
                        transport:
                          type: string
                          enum: [streamable-http, sse, stdio]
                          default: streamable-http
                    tools:
                      type: array
                      minItems: 0
                      description: |
                        Inline tool schemas. REQUIRED for Lambda and openApiSchema target
                        types. OPTIONAL for native mcpServer targets (endpoint starts with
                        https:// + transport is streamable-http/sse) — the remote MCP server
                        declares its own tools via the MCP handshake.
                      items:
                        type: object
                        required: ["name", "description", "inputSchema"]
                        properties:
                          name:
                            type: string
                            minLength: 1
                          description:
                            type: string
                          inputSchema:
                            type: object
                            required: ["type"]
                            x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                            properties:
                              type:
                                type: string
                    gatewayIdentifier:
                      type: string

# ── Custom (escape valve) ──
                # Genuine escape hatch: preserve-unknown-fields lets a sibling
                # operator round-trip arbitrary provider-specific config (gateway
                # ids, transports, region, per-tool schema) without a CRD bump.
                # Without this, K8s silently strips any field beyond the four typed
                # ones below, making `custom` admission-only paperwork.
                custom:
                  type: object
                  description: "Provider-specific configuration when provider=custom (a non-AgentCore tool backend). Open-contract escape hatch realized by a sibling operator; fields are provider-defined. Exactly one provider block must match spec.provider (CEL-enforced)."
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                  properties:
                    baseUrl: { type: string, example: "https://tools.example.com/mcp" }
                    authHeader: { type: string }
                    authSecretRef: { type: string }
                    protocol:
                      type: string
                      enum: [mcp, openapi, custom]
                      example: mcp

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
            # STATUS
            # ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
            status:
              type: object
              x-kubernetes-validations:
                # globalResourceEndpoint immutability rule deferred — the field is
                # still being shaped (path scheme, scope semantics) and operator drift
                # corrections need to land. Re-add once a stable contract is published.
                # Enforced: CEL has no warn modality, so this rule hard-rejects. The
                # operator MUST write phase + globalResourceEndpoint in the same
                # patch.status call.
                - rule: |
                    !has(self.phase) || self.phase != 'Approved' || has(self.globalResourceEndpoint)
                  message: "status.globalResourceEndpoint must be set when phase=Approved (operator must write both in the same status patch)"
                # ── Claim-verification admission CEL invariants ──
                # Deferred: globalResourceEndpoint scope vs consumers.
                #   Activate once status.boundPublicConsumers (list) is added.
                #   Intent: refuse Approved + endpointScope=mesh when public-vantage
                #   consumers are bound. K8s CEL rejects unknown structural-schema
                #   field paths even when has()-guarded, so this rule lands with the field.
                # Deferred: IdentityProvisioned=True ↔ non-empty
                #   status.identityConfigRef. Activate once identityConfigRef is
                #   promoted into the status schema. Until then operator-owned.
              properties:
                # ── Operator handler diagnostics ──
                # Status fields where the reconciling operator publishes per-handler results.
                # Declared explicitly (not preserve-unknown-fields) so mistyped status keys are rejected.
                reconcile:
                  type: object
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                  description: Operator handler result for reconcile() — diagnostic, not API surface.
                resync_from_registry:
                  type: object
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true

description: Operator handler result for resync_from_registry() — diagnostic, not API surface.
                scan_orphan_records:
                  type: object
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                  description: Operator handler result for scan_orphan_records() — diagnostic, not API surface.
                cleanup:
                  type: object
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                  description: Operator handler result for cleanup() — diagnostic, not API surface.
                phase:
                  type: string
                  # Reviewing added between Pending and Approved.
                  # Phase machines intentionally differ per asset kind: a tool is
                  # wired into a backing gateway after governance passes, so
                  # Approved (governance passed) and Active (gateway target wired,
                  # serving) are distinct states.
                  enum: [Pending, Reviewing, Approved, Active, Failed, Paused, Retired]
                reason: { type: string, maxLength: 512 }
                observedGeneration: { type: integer }
                lastReconciled: { type: string, format: date-time }
                gatewayTargetId: { type: string }
                registryRecordId:
                  type: string
                  description: "Governance-registry record key. Convention: <provider>_<asset_id>, both halves normalized (lowercase, '_'->'-', leading-alpha). Unified pattern across ModelConfig/ToolConfig/AgentConfig."
                  pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*_[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
                registryApprovalStatus:
                  type: string
                  description: "Observed registry state from timer-driven resync."
                  enum: [APPROVED, DRAFT, PENDING, DEPRECATED, MISSING, UNKNOWN]
                # ── Registry backing reference (status mirror) ──
                registryBackingRef:
                  type: object
                  description: "Observed backing that received this asset's record at last reconcile."
                  properties:
                    name:
                      type: string
                      description: "Registry CR name that was resolved."
                    backing:
                      type: string

description: "Backing kind (agentcore | tmf639 |...)."
                    recordId:
                      type: string
                      description: "Backing-specific record id (e.g., AgentCore recordId)."
                    observedAt:
                      type: string
                      format: date-time
                registryLastObserved:
                  type: string
                  format: date-time
                  description: "Wall-clock time of last resync from registry (@timer every 5 min)."
                driftDetected:
                  type: boolean
                  description: "True when CR state contradicts registry state."
                driftReason:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 256
                  description: "Human-readable explanation when driftDetected=true."
                tmf639ResourceId:
                  type: string
                  description: "TMF639 Resource ID from Canvas Resource Inventory v5."
                daysUntilRetirement: { type: integer }
                safetyEnabled: { type: boolean }
                # ── Governance perimeter URL ──
                # The operator writes status.endpoint; this property MUST be
                # declared here or K8s silently strips the write — every status
                # field an operator sets needs a matching schema declaration.
                endpoint:
                  type: string
                  description: "Governed runtime URL agents MUST call. Per-wire-format path (e.g. .../mcp/<alias>). Status-driven discovery clients read THIS, not upstreamEndpoint, to stay on the governed path."
                # Per-scope governed endpoint map {scope: url} the operator publishes
                # via the shared perimeter-URL helper. Open object (dynamic scope keys)
                # — declared so K8s does not silently strip the operator's write.
                endpoints:
                  type: object
                  description: "Per-scope governed endpoint URLs the operator resolved for this asset. The single best one is mirrored to status.endpoint."
                  x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                upstreamEndpoint:
                  type: string

description: "Raw provider URL behind the gateway (AgentCore Gateway MCP URL). Diagnostics only — agents that call this directly bypass MoDaaS governance and enforcement."
                # ── PDP policy projection ──
                # Operator writes status.access.pdpPolicyId after projecting the
                # inline cedarPolicy into the PDP-watched ConfigMap. Declared here
                # so K8s does not silently strip the write at default verbosity.
                access:
                  type: object
                  description: "Observed access-enforcement state for this tool."
                  properties:
                    pdpPolicyId:
                      type: string
                      maxLength: 253
                      description: |
                        Cedar policyId the operator projected to the in-cluster PDP
                        (label-scoped ConfigMap in modaas-system). Empty when no
                        inline access.cedarPolicy is declared. The AI Gateway tool
                        path sends this id in POST <pdp>/decide.
                # ── Global Resource Endpoint + scope ──
                globalResourceEndpoint:
                  type: string
                  format: uri
                  description: |
                    Stable, externally-resolvable URL representing the governance perimeter
                    for this asset. Set by operator on transition to Approved. Immutable
                    thereafter. Format: https://<gateway-host>/<wire-format>/<asset-uid>.
                endpointScope:
                  type: string
                  enum: [mesh, vpc, public]
                  description: |
                    Resolvable scope of globalResourceEndpoint. mesh = cluster-internal only;
                    vpc = VPC-internal; public = externally addressable.
                componentRef:
                  type: object
                  description: "Canvas Component CR that owns this asset (set by operator after Component emission)."
                  properties:
                    name:
                      type: string
                    namespace:
                      type: string
                    uid:
                      type: string
                tmf639Resource:
                  type: object

description: "TMF639 v5 Resource Inventory record this asset projects to."
                  properties:
                    id:
                      type: string
                      description: "Stable TMF639 resource ID."
                    url:
                      type: string
                      format: uri
                      description: "Direct URL to the TMF639 record (e.g., RI baseUrl + /resource/{id})."
                audit:
                  type: object
                  description: "Addressable audit pointers for this asset."
                  properties:
                    logGroup:
                      type: string
                      description: "CloudWatch log group name."
                    queryUrl:
                      type: string
                      format: uri
                      description: "Pre-built CloudWatch Logs Insights query URL."
                # ── Adopt vs Managed mode observability ──
                managed:
                  type: boolean
                  description: "True if operator created the Gateway target (managed mode); false if adopted."
                gatewayIdentifier:
                  type: string
                  description: "The Gateway hosting the target (set in both managed and adopt modes)."
                observedTools:
                  type: array
                  description: "Tools observed on the adopted Gateway target (adopt mode only). Populated from get_gateway_target."
                  items:
                    type: object
                    x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
                    properties:
                      name: { type: string }
                      description: { type: string }
                # ── Governance approval audit trail ──
                governance:
                  type: object
                  description: "Governance approval state (Reviewing → Approved gate)."
                  properties:
                    approvals:
                      type: array
                      description: "Append-only list of signed approval attestations."
                      items:
                        type: object
                        required: [subject, role, at]
                        properties:
                          subject: { type: string, maxLength: 253 }

This document describes the design artefacts for the AI-Native Canvas part of the [overall ODA Canvas design](Canvas-design.md).

There is an introductory video at

[![AI-Native-Canvas-video](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/End-to-end%20AI%20Native%20Canvas%20architecture.PNG)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MICzwN8VB_o)

The AI-Native Canvas extends the Open Digital Architecture (ODA) to support AI-native systems at enterprise scale. This work addresses three critical questions:

1. How do we expose ODA Components as tools for AI agents using MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
2. How can we deploy AI agents themselves as modular, composable components?
3. How do we operate a multi-vendor, multi-agent architecture at scale while maintaining governance, security, and responsible AI practices?

Three key Catalyst programs from 2025 significantly influenced the AI-Native Canvas approach:

* [Agent Fabric Catalyst](https://www.tmforum.org/catalysts/projects/C25.0.798/agent-fabric-phase-ii) 
* [Agentic ODA for Personalized Customer Experiences](https://www.tmforum.org/catalysts/projects/C25.0.793/agentic-oda-for-proactive-personalized-customer-experiences)
* [Growing B2B with Autonomous Agents](https://www.tmforum.org/catalysts/projects/M25.0.797/Growing-B2B-with-autonomous-agents)

These Catalyst proof-of-concepts revealed several critical patterns:

1. **AI agents as architectural paradigm**: Modular, task-oriented, context-aware systems operating autonomously within defined guardrails
2. **MCP as standard**: The de facto standard for how agents use APIs as tools, with TM Forum Open APIs well-suited for MCP wrappers
3. **Multi-agent architectures**: Modular agents collaborating to deliver use cases, with tightly scoped agents outperforming general-purpose ones
4. **Cross-layer applicability**: Agents relevant across every architectural layer and throughout the technology lifecycle

The existing component patterns already include a declarative model for exposing API services. Components expose multiple APIs beyond TM Forum functional APIs, supporting cross-industry standards like OpenMetrics and OpenTelemetry. Extending components to expose MCP APIs was as simple as expanding the enumeration to include MCP.

![Component-exposing-MCP](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Component%20exposing%20MCP%20tools%20interface.PNG)

MCP requires special handling because it uses an event-based architecture with long-running HTTP connections rather than standard REST-style integration. This means API Gateways need special configuration to support these persistent connections.

The Canvas has been extended to:

* Allow declarative specification of MCP interface types in the component model
* Build MCP operators to automatically configure API Gateways for long-running connections
* Implement MCP servers for ODA Components (e.g., Product Catalog Management)

![MCP-tools-example](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Component%20MCP%20tools%20example.PNG)

MCP is fundamentally about describing APIs in natural language so agents understand how to use them. The most important part of MCP implementation is the English description of both the API function and all arguments. This contrasts sharply with Swagger descriptions, which were designed for API experts, not AI agents.

Key implementation findings:

* Arguments require detailed explanation and examples
* Language models work better with specific examples in the descriptions
* Filtering and complex parameters need explicit examples for agents to use them effectively

The API workstream has recognized that MCP wrappers could be generated automatically from Swagger files by upgrading descriptions with more detail and examples, assuming these Swaggers might be consumed by language models.

heading_path: Agents Packaged as Composable ODA Components
chunks.text:
![Agentic-component-assumptions](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Agentic%20components%20-%20assumptions.PNG)

The extension of the component model to support agents is based on several key assumptions:

1. **Foundational models as services**: GenAI models and classical machine learning models execute as services accessed through APIs on the underlying cloud platform. Agent software accesses language models through APIs, consistent with most agent frameworks today.

2. **Approved model catalogs**: CSPs will maintain approved catalogs of foundational GenAI models. This is standard practice - for example, at Vodafone, the common platform requires any language model to be on an approved list, with a rigorous process for adding new models while maintaining privacy and security standards.

3. **Non-deterministic systems**: Agentic components are non-deterministic, requiring significantly more testing. The preferred term is "evaluation" - components need comprehensive evaluation datasets and metrics to continuously evaluate agent performance against expectations.

heading_path: Agents Packaged as Composable ODA Components
chunks.text: 4. **Additional canvas services**: Agent components typically require additional cloud services like vector databases, anonymization services, and chunking services, which need to be available in the Canvas.

heading_path: Agents Packaged as Composable ODA Components
chunks.text:
![Extending-component-model](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Extending%20component%20model%20to%20enable%20agentic%20components.PNG)

The component model extension originated from the "Agentic ODA for Proactive Customer Experiences" Catalyst. The approach allows components to declare which language models they want to access, providing a prioritized list. The Canvas platform then grants access to whichever subset are available in the approved language models.

Similar to `exposedAPIs` and `dependentAPIs`, the specification includes `dependentModels`, where components:

* Describe the models and their priority
* Provide details about the use case (required for use case inventory)
* Define guardrails to ensure responsible AI usage

The declarative requirements allow components to define their thresholds against guardrails as well.

heading_path: Agents Packaged as Composable ODA Components
chunks.text:
![AIVA-example](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/AIVA%20as%20example%20Agentic%20component.PNG)

The implementation was showcased at DTW using AIVA (TM Forum AI Assistant) packaged as a component and deployed on the Canvas. As an API-first component, AIVA was tested through direct API integration (not through the AIVA portal), allowing other agents to communicate directly with AIVA through APIs.

![AIVA-workflow](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/AIVA%20as%20example%20Agentic%20component%20-%20workflow.PNG)

Deploying AIVA on the Canvas provided immediate use of all existing Canvas services:

* Modular deployment
* API exposure through API Gateway
* Observability
* Identity management

These capabilities come standard when deploying agents as software components and are essential for any agent deployment.

heading_path: Agents Packaged as Composable ODA Components
chunks.text:
To grant access to foundational GenAI models, the Canvas introduces an **AI Gateway**. When granting access to unknown models, access is provided through this gateway (or proxy), which enables:

* **Auditing**: All interactions are audited, essential for responsible AI practices
* **Observability**: Exact monitoring of what's being discussed between components, agents, and underlying language models
* **Cost management**: Understanding how many tokens of which model a component is consuming

The process follows four steps:

1. An operator reads the declarative requirements
2. Configures the AI Gateway
3. Grants the component access with authentication and input details for accessing language models
4. Enforces guardrails while providing data for auditing, observability, and cost management

This forms the foundation for what the Canvas must provide to support multi-vendor AI agents across every functional domain, enabling governance, control, and responsible AI adoption at scale.

heading_path: Canvas Services to Support AI Agents at Scale
chunks.text:
![Canvas-AI-Capabilities](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Canvas%20AI%20Capabilities.PNG)

For multi-vendor AI agents across every functional domain, the Canvas needs:

chunks.text:

* **Other AI models**: Embedding models, multimodal models
* **Classical ML models**: With correspondent MLOps processes

A Canvas registry with tagging of:

![End-to-end-architecture](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/End-to-end%20AI%20Native%20Canvas%20architecture.PNG)

The AI-Native Canvas fits within the end-to-end AI and data architecture through collaboration between the Composable IT mission (where Canvas and Component work resides) and the AI and Data mission.

![Canvas-pre-AI](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Canvas%20pre%20AI.PNG)

Historically, composable IT within ODA consisted of:

* **Modular standard components**: Extensive work building components with use cases and Catalyst programs
* **ODA Canvas**: Operators read component requirements and configure underlying cloud platform services
* **Foundational services**: API Gateways, service meshes, observability, identity and access management systems

heading_path: Canvas with AI and Data Extensions
chunks.text:
![Canvas-with-AI-Data](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Canvas%20with%20AI%20and%20Data.PNG)

The AI-Native Canvas extensions add:

* **Agentic components**: Alongside standard ODA Components
* **MCP interfaces**: Components can offer MCP so they're available as tools toward other agents
* **Agent-to-Agent (A2A) standards**: Support for emerging standards like Google's A2A protocol, where agent components expose "agent cards" explaining their capabilities as part of a YAML contract in the component specification
* **AI operators**: Model operators that read declarative requirements and configure the AI Gateway
* **Data products as a service**: Future extension where components declare requirements for data products, with data operators integrating and granting access through underlying data services

The patterns already established fit naturally with these AI services. The experimentation has successfully extended the ODA Component model for agentic components.

heading_path: Canvas with AI and Data Extensions
chunks.text: **Note on standardization**: Agentic components are shown in white (vs. colored systems of record components) to indicate that, similar to engagement management, we want to enable deployment of agents as components following the component model, without requiring standardized agents. This allows non-standard agents to seamlessly interact and interrogate all systems of record components, leveraging the foundational data within TM Forum standards.

![Canvas-Resource-Inventory](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Interact%20with%20a%20Canvas%20via%20Agent.PNG)

On top of the Canvas, a resource inventory has been built that serves as a registry of components, agents, tools, and use cases. The Canvas uses the TMF639 Resource Inventory API as a standard interface, making it straightforward to expose components and APIs into a TM Forum-compliant resource inventory.

As with all TM Forum APIs, the resource inventory can be exposed as an MCP server to make it available to AI agents. This means:

* External AI agents (e.g., Claude Desktop) can integrate with the Canvas using the MCP server as a tool
* Agents can query in natural language: "What resources are available in the ODA Canvas?"
* Agents can request detailed descriptions of specific components and APIs
* Agents can even create diagrams of component architectures automatically

This enables AI agents to discover and understand the Canvas architecture, making the platform self-documenting and accessible through natural language interfaces.

In addition to GenAI models, the Canvas supports classical machine learning models through an **AI Model Manager**.

For custom machine learning models, the component needs to include that custom model as part of the component definition. Similar to how container images are specified in Kubernetes manifests, components include a URL to a machine learning model in an accessible model repository.

The Model Manager operator:

1. Downloads the model
2. Submits it into an MLOps pipeline for review, testing, and deployment
3. Once approved and deployed, provides API access to the inference engine so the component can access the custom model

This approach enables components to package and deploy their own custom ML models while maintaining proper governance and operations processes.

![Evaluation-1](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Evaluation%201.PNG)
![Evaluation-2](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Evaluation%202.PNG)
![Evaluation-3](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Evaluation%203.PNG)
![Evaluation-4](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Evaluation%204.PNG)
![Evaluation-5](images/AI-Native%20Canvas/Evaluation%205.PNG)

Because AI services are non-deterministic, components should come packaged with complete evaluation datasets and tests.

* **Pre-deployment**: Conduct comprehensive evaluation to establish baseline performance for the agent
* **In production**: Continuously evaluate and monitor agent behavior and characteristics

For the AIVA agent component:

1. **Golden dataset**: Created 87 evaluation questions representing the types of questions someone might ask the TM Forum AI Assistant
2. **Usage logging**: During real usage, log user questions and AIVA responses, gathering information about what people are actually asking
3. **Evaluation questions and responses**: Create evaluation datasets with AIVA responses for automatic and human-based manual evaluation

**AI-based evaluation**: At scale in production, use AI-based evaluators to evaluate AIVA's performance and responses using frameworks like the LangGraph open-source evaluation framework. The AI evaluator uses prompt templates:

* "You are an expert evaluator"
* Provides the question and answer
* Asks the AI model to evaluate for relevance, accuracy, completeness
* Provides overall assessment

**Human evaluation**: Built an interface for human evaluators to score responses for:

* Relevance
* Accuracy
* Completeness
* Commentary on scoring rationale

The evaluation framework provides:

* Metrics distinguishing golden questions vs. user questions
* Tracking of manual vs. automatic AI evaluation
* Dashboard to monitor agent performance over time
* Ensuring changes improve overall performance before deployment

This continuous evaluation is essential for maintaining quality in non-deterministic AI systems and provides the confidence needed for production enterprise deployments.
The AI-Native Canvas demonstrates that the Open Digital Architecture isn't just ready for AI - it's architected to make AI operationally viable at telecommunications scale.

* **MCP integration**: Components can expose MCP interfaces, making them available as tools for AI agents
* **Agentic components**: Agents can be deployed as modular, composable components following the ODA Component model
* **Multi-agent architectures**: Support for multi-vendor, multi-agent systems with proper governance and control
* **AI Gateway**: Provides auditing, observability, and cost management for AI interactions
* **Evaluation framework**: Continuous evaluation for non-deterministic AI systems
* **Resource inventory**: Self-documenting Canvas accessible through natural language

The Canvas provides the foundation for CSPs to confidently deploy and operate multi-vendor agent architectures across every functional domain with:

* **Governance and control**: Required for enterprise scale operations
* **Responsible AI practices**: Auditing, observability, cost control, continuous evaluation
* **Regulatory compliance**: Use case registry and high-risk tagging for EU AI Act
* **Production-ready**: All the operational capabilities needed for enterprise telecommunications systems
